purpose: Extend the user's research on asymmetric strongly regular graphs; preserve verified source facts and small reproducible examples.

terminology.asymmetric: Aut(G) consists only of the identity; group order is 1, not 0.
terminology.caution: Strong regularity fixes pairwise intersection counts, not the existence of vertex permutations.

sources.title: Random strongly regular graphs?
sources.author: Peter J. Cameron
facts: In the Latin square and Steiner triple system families described in section 3, asymptotically almost all associated graphs have trivial automorphism groups.
This is a family-specific asymptotic statement, not a uniform probability assertion over all SRGs.
In Theorem 4.3, H(S)=1 does not mean Aut(G)=1: affine translations and scalar transformations remain.

sources.title: The Steiner triple systems of order 19
sources.status: Complete STS(19) census; an injective family of SRGs, not a complete SRG(57,24,11,9) census.
sources.group_transfer: Theorem 2.5: for v>=19 the STS and block graph automorphism groups are isomorphic.
sources.correction: The older 1992 count 172248 for nontrivial automorphism groups is corrected here to 164758.

sources.title: Point configurations that are asymmetric yet balanced
facts: These are the smallest asymmetric SRGs.
The two asymmetric graphs are complements of one another.
Their spectral embeddings remain balanced despite trivial automorphism groups.

sources.title: Switching for Small Strongly Regular Graphs
sources.author: Ferdinand Ihringer
sources.status: Counts in the published switching collections, not classifications of all SRGs with these parameters.
sources.current_data_note: Author's page accessed 2026-10-14 lists larger bonus collections (96,19,2,4):1404192 and (85,20,3,5):3565042. Do not transfer the published automorphism percentages to these larger collections.

sources.title: Cycle switching in Steiner triple systems of order 19
facts: A Pasch-switch component consists of 16 STS(19), each asymmetric.
Its switching graph has automorphism group of order 256; the six-Pasch substructures have automorphism group of order 64. These are different objects from the STS and its block graph.

local_verification.srg25: Exact SRG parameters; all three K5s; intrinsic 15-vertex core has 2 automorphisms after 240 candidate checks; nonidentity fails on exterior profiles; identity fixes all 10 exterior vertices.
local_verification.srg57: Decoded published A0; verified STS19 and block graph parameters (57,24,11,9). All 5814 images of generating triple (0,1,3) tested. 10 extend to bijections, only identity preserves every triple. Group transfer by Kaski-Ostergard Theorem 2.5.
local_verification.novelty: Reproductions and new local certificates for known published graphs; not new isomorphism classes.

conway_implications: Aut(G)=1 is compatible with strong regularity, including at sizes close to 99 and with comparatively small lambda and mu.
These sources do not settle existence or asymmetry for parameters (99,14,1,2).
The eight locally collected (243,22,1,2) graphs are a structured nonexhaustive sample, not evidence for a universal symmetry theorem.
Compare how local permutations fail to extend globally in verified asymmetric controls versus the forced distance-two labels in lambda=1, mu=2.
Conway triangles form a partial Steiner triple system on 99 points, not the STS19 used above. The 57-vertex construction takes blocks as vertices, not points.
next_comparison: Use the verified 25- and 57-vertex examples as asymmetric controls; use an Ihringer (96,19,2,4) example as a size-and-sparsity control before inferring parameter-specific symmetry.
